To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the stand structure in Scots pine dominated peatland forests changes from uneven-aged and widely-spaced to uneven-aged and densely stocked, and that this change in structure is faster in southern Finland.
stand structure in drained peatland Scots pinestands develops from a natural, widely spaced structure to a structure that is similar to the structure of stands on mineral soil sites.

the natural development of stand structure on peatland sites is driven by natural processes of stand dynamics, i.e. regeneration, growth, mortality and competition, and that the stand structure becomes more even during stand succession.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the natural development of stand structure following ditching, and the results can be considered to reflect the natural development of the stand structure on peatland sites.
stand development in drained pine stands in Finland.
the natural development of stand structure following drainage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the natural development of peatland Scots pines is towards even-sized and even-aged stands.
stand structure in Scots pine dominated peatland sites develops in a natural way, and the stand dynamics can be explained by the inter-tree competition within stands.

the natural development of stand structure on peatland Scots-pine dominated stands following drainage is a complex process that can be described as a gradual transition from uneven-sized to even-sized structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the stand structure on drained, natural peatland sites develops towards even-sized, dense stands, and the stand dynamics are faster in southern Finland.
the stand’s natural structural dynamics were strongly driven by inter-tree competition.
the stand structure of Scots pine dominated peatland sites develops naturally from an uneven-sized structure to more even-sized structure during the post-drainage succession.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the stand’s initial structure and the subsequent change in stand dynamics are important factors to consider when planning silvicultural treatments on drained peatlands.
stand structure in Scots pine dominated drained peatlands develops naturally towards a bell-shaped DBH distribution, which is a typical feature of mature stands in productive sites.
natural stand development in drained peatland Scots pines can be predicted by the stand’s structural dynamics.
